srs.title: SRS Overview: UPI Payments Application for Bank Customers
srs.summary: This system will enable bank customers to perform UPI-based fund transfers and merchant payments via QR codes and UPI IMPS/NEFT channels. The application must enforce flat daily transaction limits per user and integrate a fraud monitoring system to detect suspicious behavioral patterns (e.g., high-
assumptions: Users have access to a UPI-enabled mobile device and a linked bank account.
The bank's backend systems (core banking, card networks) are available and can be integrated for transaction processing and limit enforcement.
Stakeholders agree on the 'flat cap per user per day' rule for transaction limits without needing further definition of the cap amount or per-transaction limits.
stakeholders: End Users: Bank customers sending/receiving money.
Bank Operations/Digital Banking Team: For managing user limits and accessing Head of Digital Banking authority workflows.
Fraud Risk Management Team: For defining rules, monitoring alerts, and investigating suspicious transactions.
Head of Digital Banking: The sole authority approving fraud rule changes and limit adjustments.
Regulatory Bodies (e.g., RBI): As per reference evidence regarding fraud monitoring and security standards.

requirements.statement: The system shall support two transaction channels: QR code scanning and UPI IMPS/NEFT.
requirements.acceptance: Users can successfully initiate a payment by scanning a merchant QR code and by selecting UPI IMPS/NEFT from the channel list.

requirements.statement: The system shall enforce a flat cap per user per day for transaction limits.
requirements.acceptance: The system rejects any single transaction attempt that exceeds the configured flat daily cap for the specific user.

requirements.statement: The system shall block user access after 10 consecutive failed log-in or authentication attempts.
requirements.acceptance: Access to the app is automatically blocked immediately after the 10th failed attempt, and a notification is sent to the customer.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a secure procedure for users to re-activate access after a block due to failed attempts.
requirements.acceptance: The user receives an alert explaining the block and a secure verification method (e.g., OTP, facial scan) to successfully restore access.

requirements.statement: The system shall log and alert the Head of Digital Banking for any attempt to modify fraud rules or transaction limits.
requirements.acceptance: Requests for rule or limit changes require digital authorization from the designated Head of Digital Banking before implementation.

requirements.statement: The system shall monitor transaction velocity, new beneficiary additions, and high-risk merchant codes to detect suspicious behavior.
requirements.acceptance: The system generates a real-time alert to the customer whenever a transaction triggers a pre-defined parameter for suspicious behavior (e.g., velocity spike).

requirements.statement: The system shall ensure no customer card details are stored in plain text within the app or vendor systems.
requirements.acceptance: Security audit scans reveal zero instances of card details stored in plain text across the system and vendor environments.

requirements.statement: The system shall implement a 24x7 monitoring mechanism for breach incidents with a defined response workflow.
requirements.acceptance: The system logs all breach attempts and executes a predefined incident response protocol within 15 minutes of detection, seven days a week.

requirements.statement: The system shall validate Point of Sale (PoS) terminals against PCI-P2PE standards and encrypt data instantly upon swipe.
requirements.acceptance: The system rejects merchant PoS terminals not validated against PCI-P2PE and ensures data transmission is encrypted before leaving the terminal.

requirements.statement: The system shall utilize behavioral biometrics and geo-location analysis to detect account generation or vishing fraud.
requirements.acceptance: The system flags transactions originating from new accounts, unusual geo-locations, or patterns consistent with vishing for further review.
